subject: APAC pilot — operationalizing model-improvement opt-out and export path
messages:
From: Sophie Tan <sophie.tan@aurichealth-apac.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0800
Subject: Aurora pilot — operational asks on no-improve and exports

Hi Ethan,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving ahead with a small APAC pilot (clinical triage) and have a couple of legal/ops asks before we sign the pilot SOW: primarily around the no-model-improvement (no-train) commitment and how you would operationalize exports/residency for APAC data.

High level questions:
- Can Redwood commit in the DPA to a model-improvement exclusion for Auric pilot data (no use for model training or tuning)?
- What evidence can you provide that the data is not used for model improvement (logs, export snapshots, proof-of-absence for training pipelines)?
- For APAC residency, do you support an onshore forwarding path (SFTP or API) to our Singapore tenant; what's the expected RTO and how do you guarantee no cross-border copies?

I've attached our draft DPA + controls matrix to this note. I copied Liam (IT lead) and Min (legal) — Min will be the point for contractual redlines.

Can you outline operational steps and approximate timelines for the evidence pack we typically ask for? We're trying to keep the pilot window tight (target start: early Jan).

Thanks,
Sophie

--
Sophie Tan
Head of Risk & Compliance | Auric Health (APAC)
Sophie.Tan@aurichealth-apac.com
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tan <sophie.tan@aurichealth-apac.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:04:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Aurora pilot — operational asks on no-improve and exports

Hi Sophie — thanks for sharing the draft DPA and the control matrix. Looping David (Privacy/Legal ops) and Marissa (Customer Success/Onboarding) so we can give a single operational plan.

Quick answers up front:
- Yes, we can agree to a no-model-improvement commitment scoped to pilot tenant/data in the DPA (we typically implement this as a contractual "no-use-for-model-improvement" clause + an operational toggle to prevent telemetry from entering learning pipelines).
- Evidence: we provide a short evidence pack that includes: service config snapshot (no-improve toggle on), token-level telemetry extract (sampling), routing logs showing onshore egress, and a signed operational attestation. For higher assurance, we can also run a one-time export of relevant interaction logs to your SFTP for independent verification.
- Residency: we support a dedicated APAC routing policy and can configure onshore exports to your SG SFTP tenant. RTO for the export job is normally within 48 hours for a one-off snapshot; continuous replication is possible but requires additional config/contracting. We will not persist copies outside the configured onshore lane for pilot traffic when the no-improve toggle is active.

Action items we'll take next:
1) David: confirm list of evidence artifacts we will produce and any redaction considerations for PHI.
2) Marissa: outline onboarding schedule and SFTP connectivity checklist.
3) Ethan (me): produce an ops checklist and sample attestation for your legal review.

We'll aim to put a 1-week draft evidence bundle together once you confirm the exact pilot tenant and SFTP endpoint. Can Min share the preferred format for the attestation and any particular exportability proof you need (e.g., hash manifests, signed manifests)?

Best,
Ethan

--
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ethan_park@redwood.com
From: Min Chen <min.chen@auric-health-legal.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:22:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Aurora pilot — operational asks on no-improve and exports

Ethan / team,

Thanks — attached is our redlined DPA (Auric_DPA_draft_v1.pdf) and a short controls matrix (Auric_Controls_Matrix.xlsx). A few clarifications from legal ops:

1) Scope of no-improve: We need the commitment to explicitly include user prompts and generated model outputs. Also need confirmation that any downstream subprocessor (log analytics, backup providers) are bound to the same scope.

2) Evidence: please confirm whether Redwood can provide the following items as part of the evidence pack:
   - A service-config export showing no-improve flag (with UTC timestamp)
   - A time-bounded token telemetry extract for pilot tenant (redacted PHI allowed)
   - A routing log proving traffic stayed within SG region (or list of public IP blocks)
   - A signed manifest (SHA256) of the export files we receive

3) On subprocessor commitments: We expect a list of subprocessors touching the data and confirmation they are contractually prohibited from using the pilot data for model improvement.

4) On transfers/backups: Are there any automatic backups or audit snapshots that might replicate data outside SG (e.g., to a central analytics cluster)? If so, we need mitigation steps and a timeline to remove or segregate those snapshots.

Please respond with an operational timeline that maps to our pilot target (start of Jan).

Regards,
Min Chen
Senior Counsel | Auric Health
min.chen@auric-health-legal.com

--- Attached: Auric_DPA_draft_v1.pdf; Auric_Controls_Matrix.xlsx
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Min Chen <min.chen@auric-health-legal.com>, Sophie Tan <sophie.tan@aurichealth-apac.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Aurora pilot — operational asks on no-improve and exports

Min / Sophie — thanks for the redlines. Below is an operational plan and timeline we can commit to for the pilot. Marissa will follow up with the onboarding calendar.

Operational evidence pack (deliverables):
- Config snapshot: service-config-auric-20261117.json (captures tenant flags including no-improve toggle, KMS routing) — provided within 3 business days of request.
- Token telemetry extract: time-bounded CSV (fields: timestamp, anonymized_session_id, token_count, prompt_length, prompt_hash) — redacted for PHI per your guidance; delivered within 5 business days.
- Routing logs: flow logs + IP range mapping for the pilot window; delivered within 5 business days.
- Signed export manifest: SHA256 checksums for every file we export; generated at export time and signed by our operational PGP key.
- Subprocessor attestation: list of subprocessors and a signed attestation that none will use the pilot data for model improvement; delivered with the evidence pack.

Operational constraints and mitigations:
- Backups: For pilot traffic we will disable cross-region replication for any analytic snapshots. Where immutable backups are part of infra, we will isolate pilot data into a segregated snapshot lifecycle and provide an autodestruction policy (delete after 30 days unless otherwise agreed).
- KMS: Keys used for onshore export can be customer-managed in SG (we support bringing your KMS via standard key import or an HSM-backed VPN session); we will document the key wrapping flows in the evidence pack.

Timeline (targeting Pilot start early Jan):
- Week 1 (now): Confirm SFTP endpoint + legal format for attestation. Finalize scope of redlines in the DPA.
- Week 2: Provision routing policy, enable no-improve toggle for a dedicated pilot tenant, run a smoke export to your SFTP (test file) and share manifest.
- Week 3: Produce full evidence pack (config snapshot, telemetry extract, routing logs, subprocessor attestation).
- Week 4 (if needed): Address any follow-ups or audits requested by Auric.

Next steps: Sophie / Min — please share the SFTP endpoint (host, path, PGP key or username) and confirm that the manifest SHA256 + PGP signature meets your internal verification. Once we have that, Marissa will schedule the connectivity window.

I'll attach our internal checklist for no-improve pilots to the thread (redwood-no-improve-evidence-checklist.xlsx).

Best regards,
David Kim
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com
